title: accordion-burst-lab-log-karen
content:
Goal:
- Explore an "accordion" arrival pattern: repeated short high-amplitude bursts separated by brief low-traffic troughs. Hypothesis is that alternating compression/expansion of request pressure exposes warm/cold-cache penalty asymmetry and kernel-path thrash (e.g., quantized path vs fp16 switchovers).

Experiment notes (quick):
- Model: rwd-v2-small-8q (8-bit quantized candidate) on a single A100-80GB node in dev-fleet.
- Runtime config: continuous-batching=on, kv_cache_enabled=on, batch_timeout_ms=6, max_concurrency=32, prefetch_workers=4
- Traffic driver: custom harness (nodejs) that emits an accordion waveform: 3s burst @ 120 qps, 2s lull @ 8 qps, repeated for 30 minutes. Script: ./tools/driver --pattern accordion --burst_qps 120 --lull_qps 8 --burst_dur 3 --lull_dur 2 --duration 1800
- Payload: synthetic prompt, avg tokens in/out = 160/60, small temperature.
- Instrumentation: per-request trace IDs, token-level timing, kv-cache hit/miss logs, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi at 1s), CPU sys/idle, host-level iowait.

Raw observations (first pass):
- Mean QPS reported: 74 (expected ~ (3*120 + 2*8)/5 = 76.8, small driver jitter).
- GPU util oscillates: ~92% during bursts, ~28% during lulls.
- KV cache hit rate: drops ~7% at the start of each burst, then recovers over ~1.1s. Suggests partial cache evaporation during lull windows.
- Tail latencies (p99) spike dramatically on the first burst after a lull: median p99 during spikes = 780ms, steady bursts p99 = 240ms, lull p99 = 150ms.
- p50/p95/p99 samples (aggregated by phase):
  - Burst (warm): p50 48ms, p95 180ms, p99 240ms
  - Burst (first 800ms after lull): p50 140ms, p95 410ms, p99 780ms
  - Lull: p50 44ms, p95 120ms, p99 150ms

ASCII mini-chart (p99 over time, indexes represent 5s windows):
  [|||||||||||||====|==============|====|||||||||||]
  Legend: | = high p99 region, = = low p99 region (shows repeated spike then decay).

Debug traces (sample):
- trace-2026-02-28-10:02: first request of burst after lull. Timeline:
  - client->proxy 4ms
  - proxy queue wait 22ms (queue flushed)
  - runtime cold path entry 86ms (kernel-switch + kvcache-miss)
  - model forward first token 150ms
  - total 762ms
  Notes: cold-path entry aligns to a kvcache miss and a quantized-kernel rebind that takes ~60-90ms.

Hypotheses / root cause candidates:
1) KV cache partial eviction during lull windows (client-level context windows are small; runtime frees parts of prefix when GPU mem pressure drops) leading to warm penalties when bursts resume.
2) OS-level process scheduling: during lull, worker threads become idle and underlying CUDA contexts enter a lower-power mode; first wakeups have extra latency (observed small CPU wake delay + cuda context warm).
3) Kernel path reshuffle: runtime switches between low-latency fused kernels vs. quantized vectorized kernels based on instantaneous batch sizes; the decision boundary oscillates causing extra setup cost at transition times.

Quick experiments to isolate causes (planned next runs):
- Keep KV cache pinned across lull (disable auto-evict) and rerun accordion to see if first-burst spike disappears.
- Force constant small background traffic during lull (5 qps steady) to prevent thread/process idle and see delta.
- Remove quantized path (force fp16 path) to observe if kernel rebinding is main culprit.
- Increase batch_timeout_ms to 12 to smooth batching decisions; expect lower p99 spikes at cost of slightly higher p50.

Preliminary takeaways:
- Accordion patterns (short burst / short lull) are worse than continuous bursts with equivalent mean QPS: tail penalties are concentrated on burst boundaries. For customer workloads that have interleaved user activity (mobile clients sync, then rest), this matters.
- Two low-friction mitigations to try first: 1) maintain small background keepalive traffic to prevent chains of cold transitions, 2) knob to pin kvcache across short lull windows. Both are low-risk and likely help while we pursue more structural fixes.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Run pin-cache experiment (disable-evict flag) TOMORROW morning 09:30; tag run with JIRA-RT-867-pin
- Add metric: per-key kvcache TTL and eviction count in telemetry (currently opaque).
- Check kernel-selection logs in more verbose mode to capture transition timestamps (enable --kernel-debug).
- Discuss with Maya about adding a synthetic "accordion" test to daily smoke suite if results persist.
- Draft short customer-facing note for platform team: "observed high tail on short-burst patterns; recommended keepalive and kvcache pinning".

Random scribbles (ideas):
- Could prefetch common prefix tokens at lull end (speculative prefix fill) to amortize warm penalty.
- Add adaptive background heartbeat: detect lull and optionally simulate a tiny request that primes cache before user-initiated burst. Need to evaluate cost tradeoffs.

End of log.

Appendix: driver command (for reproducibility):
./tools/driver \
  --pattern accordion \
  --burst_qps 120 --lull_qps 8 \
  --burst_dur 3 --lull_dur 2 \
  --payload templates/synthetic-short.json \
  --headers "x-experiment:accordion-pin-test" \
  --trace-prefix trace-accordion-20260228 \
  --out telemetry/accordion-20260228.json

Saved telemetry: telemetry/accordion-20260228.json (raw traces + aggregated windows).

If anything, keep this file as notebook-y. Will extract key graphs into a PR for infra if pinning proves positive.
